newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to free female Palestinian prisoners today.
newsitem.headline: Israel to free female Palestinian prisoners today.

text.p: Israel will free 31 female Palestinian prisoners on Tuesday as part of its peace agreements with the PLO, Israeli police and Palestinian officials said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will receive most of the prisoners in the West Bank town of Ramallah, a PLO official said.
"Thirty-one Palestinian women will be released today, 25 from Hasharon prison and six from Naveh Tirza prison," an Israeli police spokeswoman said.

PLO official Hisham Abdel Razek told Reuters that after the release one female Palestinian prisoner would remain behind bars in Israel -- a 15-year-old arrested only two weeks ago after attempting to stab an Israeli soldier.
"We will continue to demand her release," Abdel Razek, head of the prisoners committee of the Palestinian Authority, said in Gaza.
He said 28 of the women were convicted by Israeli courts of security offences and three were jailed for criminal activity unrelated to the Israel-Arab conflict.

A group of families of Israelis killed in Arab guerrilla attacks failed in a High Court bid on Monday to reverse an Israeli government decision announced on Friday to release Palestinian women prisoners.
The families argued against freeing Palestinians convicted of killing Jews. Two of the women prisoners were jailed on murder charges.
The release of female, sick and young prisoners was a commitment made in a deal signed by the previous government in September 1995 with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
Israel released some of the male sick and elderly prisoners but some 5,000 Palestinians are still in its prisons.

Regarding the women, Israeli President Ezer Weizman at first refused to pardon some of them who were involved in deadly attacks against Israelis. The female prisoners who he did pardon then chose to remain in prison in solidarity with their comrades.
An Israeli cabinet statement on Friday said the president had now decided to pardon all of the women.

In a deal with the PLO in January under which Israeli troops withdrew from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron, also fulfilling an accord signed by the prior government, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged to carry out the prisoner releases.
